Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@talentworks.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order form redlines — payment timing and VAT question

Hi Priya,

Thanks for sending over the order form redlines earlier this week. Our procurement team reviewed Legal's track changes and we have two items blocking approval on our side:

1) Payment terms — the current redline shows Net 30 but our standard is Net 60 for enterprise contracts. We can be flexible, but we need to understand if Redwood can accept Net 60 or whether there is a required commitment/fee to keep Net 30/45.

2) VAT / tax treatment — our tax team asked whether Redwood will invoice with VAT included, or if we should handle VAT via reverse charge. TalentWorks is EU-registered (we're buying through our US entity for this pilot), and we need a clear owner for VAT responsibility in the order form.

Attached the SOW and our Procurement checklist for reference. Can you confirm Redwood's position so we can move to signature?

Best,
Rajiv

Subject: Re: Order form redlines — payment timing and VAT question

Hi Rajiv — thanks for the clear note and the SOW. Looping in Kimberly (Legal) and Ben (Finance) to align.

Quick answers up front:
- Payment terms: Redwood standard is Net 30. We can consider Net 45 for strategic pilots, but Net 60 is outside our standard unless there is a commercial trade (e.g., higher minimum commit or 30% prepay).
- VAT/taxes: We typically invoice in USD from our US entity and will not add VAT on top. For EU customers that require reverse charge, we can accommodate reverse charge if TalentWorks provides the appropriate VAT registration and a tax residency certificate. Otherwise Redwood will include VAT on invoices where required by local law.

Proposed next steps:
1) Kimberly — please confirm whether Legal can add a short "tax responsibility" clause referencing customer-provided VAT evidence and reverse-charge handling.
2) Ben — can you share the revenue ops playbook for approving Net 45 vs Net 60 (what minimum commit or prepay thresholds apply)?
3) Rajiv — can TalentWorks confirm which legal entity will sign and whether you can provide VAT registration / tax residency evidence if you prefer reverse charge?

If helpful, we can propose two clean options in the order form: (A) Net 45 with current min-commit, or (B) Net 60 with 30% upfront payment and a small financing fee. Let me know which route you prefer and we'll update the redline.

Thanks — Priya
Priya Natarajan

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 11:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order form redlines — payment timing and VAT question

Thanks Priya — see proposed carveouts below that Legal recommends adding to the Order Form (we suggest inserting as a new section under 'Taxes and Invoicing'). These are intentionally concise so Procurement can review quickly: 

--- Proposed language (legal) ---
Taxes and Withholding. Customer shall be responsible for any sales, value-added, withholding or other taxes ("Taxes") imposed on Customer's purchase of Services, except for taxes based on Redwood's net income. If Customer requests that Redwood issue invoices subject to reverse charge or similar tax treatment, Customer must provide valid tax registration information and any required certificates prior to the first invoice. Unless otherwise agreed in writing, Redwood will invoice in USD.

Payment Terms. Unless otherwise agreed in writing, invoices are due Net 30 from invoice date. Redwood may agree to Net 45 upon mutual written agreement; Net 60 will require contingent commercial approval by Finance and may be conditioned on (i) an increased minimum commitment or (ii) an upfront payment equal to 30% of the first-year committed fees.

Invoice Entity. Customer shall identify the legal entity that will execute the Order Form and provide a purchase order number if required. Redwood will not be responsible for taxes or fees arising from Customer's choice of signing entity.

--- end proposed language ---

Ben — from Finance perspective, we can approve Net 45 for TW-4789 given the pilot status if they keep the minimum commit as-is. For Net 60 we would need either a 30% prepay or a 10% uplift on list pricing to cover credit exposure. Which is easier operationally?

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Priya / Kimberly / Ben — thanks for the quick turnaround and the proposed language. Couple points from our side: 

1) TalentWorks can provide VAT registration and a tax residency certificate for the EU entity. We prefer reverse charge handling (no VAT on Redwood invoice). We'll attach the certificate once legal confirms the final clause.

2) On payment terms: Net 45 would work for us for this pilot. We are not set up to do 30% prepay up front at the enterprise level for a pilot, so Net 60 with prepay is not feasible.

Next steps per your suggested options: please update the order form to include the legal clause you suggested (Taxes and Withholding) and set payment terms to Net 45. We'll review and sign once we receive the updated order form and confirm the invoice entity (TalentWorks Inc.).

Appreciate the flexibility — Rajiv
